# SafeSpace setup and verification

This guide describes the review branch in [draft PR #1](https://github.com/Yeshika0900/SafeSpace/pull/1). Run commands from the repository root unless a step changes directory. The root forwards web and native commands to `website/`.

## Install and run

Use Node **24.22.1 LTS** (tested), npm 11.9.0; tooling requires Node >=22.13. Internet is needed for initial packages and on-demand model loading. From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm --prefix website ci
npm --prefix network-agent ci
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:5173` or `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. Camera and browser Bluetooth require a secure context and user permission. Other tools remain usable if model loading fails. Images are processed locally by the model; frame capture downloads to your device. Optional second terminal:

```sh
npm run helper
```

The helper binds **127.0.0.1:4174 only**. Use it only on a computer/network you own or are authorized to inspect. It runs fixed OS commands: Windows `arp -a`, Linux `ip -4 neigh show` (fallback `arp -an` only if `ip` is missing), macOS `arp -an`. Unknown output, absent commands and timeouts produce an error, not a successful empty result. It rejects multicast/broadcast and malformed addresses; directed-broadcast handling is conservative because subnet masks are not available.

Default browser origins are exactly `http://localhost:5173`, `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, and the same hosts on preview port 4173. To use another desktop frontend, set `SAFESPACE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to a comma-separated list of exact HTTP(S) origins. Wildcards, paths, trailing slashes, credentials, missing Origin and `Origin: null` are rejected. Requests require `X-SafeSpace-Client: inventory-v1`; the website supplies it and preflight is supported. Private/local-network browser policies may still block access; HTTPS deployment is not a guarantee of helper compatibility. Origin/Host/header checks protect browser requests; **they are not authentication against arbitrary local processes or forged non-browser requests**. No pairing or account workflow is provided.

## Phone and BLE checks

The browser chooser exposes only a device you select and permitted GATT service/characteristic capabilities. **No characteristic values are read**, including serial numbers. Android native scanning observes advertisements for ten seconds and stops on tool change/background. Camera permission/model loading and GATT operations can be cancelled by stopping/leaving the tool. Neither mode guarantees tracker detection. iOS browser Bluetooth support is limited; use the OS's built-in unwanted-tracking alerts.

On a phone, localhost means the **phone**, not your laptop. Laptop network inventory is unsupported on the phone. Never expose the helper to the LAN/internet to work around this. HTTPS/device provisioning for camera/BLE must be tested separately; a laptop LAN HTTP URL is not a secure context on a phone.

## Validation

From the repository root:

```sh
npm run format:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run bundle:check
cd website
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:browser
```

Unit/component/helper/browser suites use synthetic media, GATT and network fixtures. No physical sensing is allowed in CI. TypeScript strictly checks **all eight service/data modules**, including model configuration, records, persistence, cancellation and BLE/network boundaries. React JSX, Node helper and benchmark scripts are linted/tested but are not type-checked. Browser tests use Chromium; hardware behavior and other browsers still need physical checks. See [implementation status](quality/implementation-status.md) and [benchmark reproduction](quality/benchmark.md).

## Android

`website/` owns Capacitor, its configuration and Android project. Root scripts only forward to it; run Capacitor commands from `website`, never from the repository root. Root duplicate Capacitor packages/configuration were removed. Install JDK 21, Android SDK platform 36, compatible build tools, platform tools and an emulator or authorized device; set `ANDROID_HOME` and configure `website/android/local.properties` locally if needed. Existing Gradle wrapper: 8.14.3; AGP: 8.13.0; min SDK: 24.

```sh
npm run build
npm run android:sync
cd website/android
bash gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:lintDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest
bash gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest
```

On Windows use `gradlew.bat`. `cap sync` copies assets and configures plugins; it does **not** validate an APK. The BLE plugin already contributes Bluetooth/scan/connect/location permissions. Inspect the **merged** manifest after a native build before drawing permission conclusions. The instrumented application ID assertion is `com.safespace.app`.

## Local storage and privacy

Checklist, the latest 30 sanitized BLE records, and friendly aliases are saved locally in browser/WebView storage. This is not encrypted app storage. Version-2 records separate advertised names from aliases; changing an alias cannot change name review. Legacy display names are retained as aliases with advertised evidence marked unknown, because their provenance cannot be recovered. Legacy characteristic values (`deviceDetails`, including serial metadata) are dropped and the sanitized history is rewritten when BLE opens. Migration limits nested arrays, strings and payload size. Valid checklist booleans survive malformed storage. Storage failures produce usable in-memory tools and visible feedback.

Clear history removes the BLE history **and aliases**, and clears the visible current record. Export contains only the current sanitized record. Downloaded JSON and captured frames remain in your downloads after clearing app history. Android `allowBackup=false` reduces backup of WebView identifiers; OEM/device-transfer behavior still requires physical verification. No automatic cloud sync, diagnostic identifier logging, account or retention feature was added.

Inspect your space. Understand what you observe.
Visual inspection · Bluetooth information · Local network context · Practical checks

SafeSpace brings four personal privacy tools into one workspace: a camera preview with common-object recognition, Bluetooth device information, this computer's recent network neighbours, and a saved room inspection checklist. It helps you review limited observations and decide what to inspect manually. **Status:** experimental local web application with Android packaging. The review branch has automated software checks and a small generic-object benchmark. Physical-device acceptance and Android APK validation remain open. **SafeSpace does not detect hidden cameras, identify trackers, or certify that a room is safe.**

See the workspace · Reviewer walkthrough · Run locally · Architecture · Measured evidence

## The workspace _Actual Chromium capture of the working application. Camera is off; no room imagery, Bluetooth identifiers or real network inventory was collected. This screen demonstrates the interface, not detection performance. [Capture provenance](docs/media/README.md)._ ## Four tools, clear boundaries | Tool | What you can do | What the observation means | | --- | --- | --- | | **Camera inspection** | Open a local preview, recognise ordinary COCO objects, download a frame | A common-object label and model confidence. It does not reveal whether an object contains a camera. | | **Bluetooth inspection** | Select one browser BLE device and inspect GATT capabilities; observe advertisements in the Android app | Device-supplied names and accessible capability metadata. Names can be spoofed; browser RSSI is unavailable. No characteristic values are read. | | **Wi-Fi inventory** | Read this computer's existing IPv4 neighbour cache through the optional loopback helper | An incomplete record of recent communication. It is neither an active network scan nor a list of surveillance devices. | | **Inspection checklist** | Work through six practical checks and save your progress locally | A record of the steps you checked. Completion does not establish room safety. | ### Follow an inspection 1. **Look at the space.** Open the camera preview if useful; capture a frame only when you have permission. Keep the model's ordinary-object scope in mind. 2. **Review device context.** Inspect a BLE device you select, or read the optional helper's partial neighbour inventory on the same computer. 3. **Use the checklist.** Follow the practical guidance and keep human judgement separate from model labels and unfamiliar device names. [Walk through the existing controls and expected states →](docs/REVIEWER_GUIDE.md)
See the checklist on a narrow screen _Responsive browser capture, not a physical-phone test. All checks are unchecked; no completed room inspection is implied._
## Engineering underneath The React workspace owns four separate tools. Strict TypeScript contracts cover eight service/data modules; camera generations, cancellation, record validation and platform adapters sit behind those boundaries. - **Camera ownership:** Stop remains usable during permission or model loading. Leaving the tool releases tracks; late results are ignored, and inference stays serialized across remounts. TensorFlow.js and COCO-SSD load when recognition is requested. - **BLE privacy:** advertised names and friendly aliases remain separate. Changing an alias cannot change the name assessment. Inspection enumerates capabilities without reading characteristic values; legacy serial metadata is removed during migration when storage is writable. - **Local helper:** exact Origin/Host checks, a required client header, fixed OS commands, subprocess limits and coalesced reads protect the loopback service. These are browser-request protections, not authentication against arbitrary local processes. - **Recoverable state:** malformed saved data and invalid helper responses stay within the affected tool. History, strings, nested metadata and response sizes are bounded. React 18 · Vite 6 · TensorFlow.js 4 / COCO-SSD 2.2.3 · TypeScript service contracts · Node.js helper · Capacitor 8 [Architecture and source map →](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) ## Measured evidence Recorded on **14 November 2026** during the quality work at [d3af967](https://github.com/Yeshika0900/SafeSpace/commit/d3af9676840c8e3006067e80887ca75645244981). These are separate software and generic-object measurements, not an overall SafeSpace accuracy score. This presentation pass does not add a new model evaluation. | Measurement | Recorded result | Scope | | --- | --- | --- | | Software regressions | **59** unit/component + **52** parser/helper checks pass | Synthetic media, GATT, storage and network fixtures; includes a harmless subprocess timeout check | | Browser verification | **7** Chromium checks pass | 320/390/768/1440 px, malformed state, export/clear, zoom, reduced motion and two axe states; not physical-device coverage | | Initial JavaScript | **2,059,548 → 203,164 bytes**; 90.14% smaller | Production entry bundle; model code is deferred. Gzip: 358.19 kB → 64,927 bytes | | Generic-object baseline | **26.79% AP50:95** on validation; **29.14%** on holdout | 16 + 16 COCO2017 images; TensorFlow.js pure-JS CPU; exact checkpoint training membership is not independently attested | | Candidate comparison | Validation AP50:95 **26.79% → 28.58%**, precision50 **94.59% → 88.89%** | Candidate changed score filtering and NMS IoU together. False positives rose 2 → 5; **candidate not adopted** | | Reproducibility | Identical labels, scores and boxes across two runs | Same checksum-frozen 32-image engineering subset; no phone runtime or hidden-camera accuracy claim | The original model settings remain in place. The subset is small, per-class support is sparse, and timing varied with shared-host contention. The eight-observation display cap did not alter these particular subset results; broader behaviour remains unproved. [Implementation status and CI evidence](docs/quality/implementation-status.md) · [Benchmark method and limits](docs/quality/benchmark.md) · [Raw predictions](docs/quality/benchmark-run2.json) · [Quality workflow](https://github.com/Yeshika0900/SafeSpace/actions/workflows/quality.yml) ## Run locally This README describes the **review branch in [draft PR #1](https://github.com/Yeshika0900/SafeSpace/pull/1)**. Until that work is merged, use the branch explicitly. There is no hosted demo or verified APK linked here. Use **Node 24.22.1 LTS** and npm 11.9.0 for the recorded setup; tooling requires Node >=22.13. ```sh git clone --branch codex/improve-existing-feature-quality https://github.com/Yeshika0900/SafeSpace.git cd SafeSpace npm ci npm --prefix website ci npm --prefix network-agent ci npm run dev ``` Open **http://localhost:5173**. Camera and browser Bluetooth require a secure context and permission. No application API key is required; model assets download on demand. For the optional inventory helper, run `npm run helper` in a second terminal on the **same computer**. It binds only to `127.0.0.1:4174`. On a phone, localhost refers to the phone. Laptop inventory is unsupported there; keep the helper on loopback. [Full setup, validation commands, Android prerequisites and troubleshooting →](docs/SETUP.md) ## Find your next step | You want to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Review the working product and its four tools | [Reviewer walkthrough](docs/REVIEWER_GUIDE.md) | | Install, run or verify the web/native project | [Setup and verification](docs/SETUP.md) | | Understand module ownership, data flow and storage | [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | | Audit software checks and unfinished acceptance work | [Implementation status](docs/quality/implementation-status.md) | | Reproduce the model comparison or inspect its assumptions | [Benchmark reproduction](docs/quality/benchmark.md) | | Check visual and claim sources for this presentation | [Media provenance](docs/media/README.md) · [Presentation notes](docs/presentation/README.md) | | Contribute or report a security issue | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Security reporting](SECURITY.md) | ## Responsible use and current limits Use the camera and optional neighbour helper only where you have permission. Images are processed locally; exports and captured frames download to your device. Checklist progress, a bounded BLE history and friendly aliases are stored in browser/WebView storage. Clear history removes saved BLE records and aliases; downloaded files remain in your downloads. [Storage details](docs/SETUP.md#local-storage-and-privacy). Android asset sync has passed; APK/lint/native tests were blocked by Gradle download and SDK/device availability. Physical camera/BLE behaviour, actual mobile permission policies, other browsers, larger independent evaluation and phone timings remain unverified. [Exact acceptance status](docs/quality/implementation-status.md). No repository-wide source license is currently declared. Dependencies, model weights and evaluation data retain their own terms; the benchmark notes record the redistribution limits. If an observation concerns you, move to safety and seek appropriate help rather than treating an empty result as clearance.

# A short SafeSpace walkthrough

Start with the [README](../README.md) and [local setup](SETUP.md). SafeSpace is an experimental four-tool privacy assistant. Review observations alongside their limitations; none of the tools certifies room safety.

## 1. Enter the workspace

Select **Start inspection**. It scrolls to and focuses the existing camera workspace, including when Camera Inspection is already selected. The feature buttons and workspace controls select the same four tools. The [desktop capture](media/camera-workspace-desktop.png) shows this actual state with the camera off; [provenance](media/README.md) explains its scope.

## 2. Camera inspection

If you have permission to use the camera in that space, choose **Enable camera**. Stop remains available during permission and model work. Once a stream opens, preview and frame capture can remain usable even if recognition cannot load. **Stop camera**, leaving the tool or hiding the page releases tracks. Results from an old inspection cannot populate the current view.

A chair or laptop label does not indicate a hidden camera. Confidence concerns the ordinary-object label, not room safety. **Capture frame** downloads a frame when valid video dimensions and a canvas context are available; before that, it can give a tool-local error. Physical camera acceptance is still open; automated lifecycle tests use fake streams/models.

## 3. Bluetooth inspection

In a compatible secure browser, **Choose and inspect a BLE device** opens the system chooser from the click. Cancellation or denied permission leaves controls usable. The selected device can expose permitted services and characteristic capabilities. Restricted services and disconnects produce partial results.

No characteristic values are read, including serial numbers. Friendly aliases remain separate from advertised names; an unnamed device remains unknown even after you name it. Browser RSSI is unavailable.

The Android application instead observes advertisements for ten seconds. Native RSSI is signal information, not distance or a surveillance verdict. Stop/background/tool-change behaviour is covered by fake-adapter tests; physical radio/permission acceptance remains unverified.

Export the latest sanitized record as JSON if needed. **Clear history** removes the visible current record, saved history and aliases. Downloaded exports remain outside app clearing. Documentation capture never invokes a chooser or observes real advertisements.

## 4. Wi-Fi inventory

Run the optional helper on the same authorized computer using the [setup instructions](SETUP.md), then choose **Refresh device inventory**. It reads the existing IPv4 neighbour cache with fixed OS commands. It neither probes devices nor inventories IPv6.

An empty cache is a valid empty result. Unknown output, missing executables, denied local-network access and timeouts stay errors. An unfamiliar address is not evidence of surveillance. Keep the helper on loopback; localhost on a phone refers to the phone, so laptop inventory is unsupported there. Documentation capture does not run the helper.

## 5. Checklist and storage

The checklist contains six practical checks. Toggle one only when it represents your own progress; state is saved locally when storage is writable. The count records steps, not room safety. The [narrow-screen capture](media/checklist-mobile.png) shows all six unchecked in an emulated browser viewport, not a physical-phone test.

Storage/quota errors leave tools usable in memory with feedback. Checklist null, BLE history containing a null record and a helper response with null devices are covered by recovery regressions. A tool boundary contains render failures.

## 6. Read the evidence

The [implementation record](quality/implementation-status.md) separates 59 unit/component, 52 helper and 7 Chromium checks from unexecuted hardware/native work. The [model comparison](quality/benchmark.md) retains the rejected candidate and the reason for preserving the baseline.

This presentation changes documentation and its assets. Screenshot controls, observations and limitations come from the existing app; it adds no demo-data mode, sensing workflow or model.

# SafeSpace architecture

SafeSpace uses React/Vite, a Capacitor Android wrapper and an optional Node loopback helper. Four components share one app shell. Typed services own cancellation, records and persistence; the helper separates fixed command execution from IPv4 parsing.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[User selects one of four tools] --> A[React app shell]
    A --> C[Camera preview and frame capture]
    A --> B[Browser GATT or native BLE advertisements]
    A --> N[IPv4 inventory client]
    A --> K[Six-step checklist]
    C --> M[Lazy local TensorFlow.js / COCO-SSD]
    B --> V[Validated metadata and aliases]
    V --> S[Browser or WebView storage]
    K --> S
    N --> H[127.0.0.1:4174 helper]
    H --> P[Fixed OS neighbour commands and parsers]
    C --> D[Local frame download]
    V --> J[Local JSON report download]
```

Model packages/weights may be requested from upstream hosts. Room frames are processed locally. The optional helper reads this computer's cache; it is not a phone-to-laptop bridge.

## Source map

| Responsibility | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Entry, shell and style | [main.jsx](../website/src/main.jsx), [App.jsx](../website/src/App.jsx), [styles.css](../website/src/styles.css) |
| Tool-local render recovery | [ToolBoundary.jsx](../website/src/ToolBoundary.jsx) |
| Camera UI and frame download | [Camera.jsx](../website/src/features/Camera.jsx) |
| Generation ownership and teardown | [camera.ts](../website/src/services/camera.ts) |
| Lazy model acquisition and settings | [inference.ts](../website/src/services/inference.ts) |
| BLE UI, history and JSON export | [BluetoothScan.jsx](../website/src/features/BluetoothScan.jsx) |
| BLE adapters, cancellation and dictionaries | [ble.ts](../website/src/services/ble.ts), [async.ts](../website/src/services/async.ts), [ble-metadata.ts](../website/src/services/ble-metadata.ts) |
| Record validation and persistence | [records.ts](../website/src/services/records.ts), [storage.ts](../website/src/services/storage.ts) |
| Network UI and bounded client | [NetworkScan.jsx](../website/src/features/NetworkScan.jsx), [network.ts](../website/src/services/network.ts) |
| Checklist and saved progress | [Checklist.jsx](../website/src/features/Checklist.jsx) |
| Loopback HTTP, OS commands and parsers | [server.js](../network-agent/server.js), [inventory.js](../network-agent/inventory.js) |
| Native project and configuration | [website/android](../website/android), [capacitor.config.json](../website/capacitor.config.json) |

## Resource ownership

Camera sessions reject stale generations. Stop/unmount/background release tracks and clear scheduled work. In-flight inference finishes before its model is disposed; serialization spans remounts. Recognition load failure leaves an available preview usable.

Browser chooser activation stays within the click. Browser GATT inspection and native advertisements have distinct labels/lifecycles. Teardown cancels bounded operations; late selections/connects/scans are disconnected or ignored. Characteristic values are not read. Physical radio behaviour still needs hardware validation.

The network client has a six-second deadline, cancellation and a streamed response-size cap before JSON parsing. The helper has a five-second/256 KiB subprocess bound, coalesced reads and a short cache. Origin/Host/header checks protect browser requests; local processes can forge those headers, so they are not authentication.

## Data and storage

All eight TypeScript service modules are strictly checked. React JSX, the Node helper and benchmark scripts are linted/tested but not type-checked. Runtime validators remain necessary for parsed JSON and external data.

Checklist booleans, the latest 30 sanitized BLE records and friendly aliases use browser/WebView local storage. Version-2 records separate advertised evidence from user labels and discard unnecessary legacy characteristic values. Storage denial can prevent persistent migration or clearing; the UI reports it. Downloads remain separate files. [Storage and backup details](SETUP.md#local-storage-and-privacy).

A tool boundary contains render failures. Missing observations, device names and neighbour entries never become a room-safety score or surveillance verdict.

## Verification boundaries

Fast gates cover synthetic regressions, service contracts, formatting/lint, build/bundle budget, advisories, Gitleaks and Chromium flows. The separate model harness uses pinned public COCO imagery and weights outside Git. CI performs no real sensing.

Hardware/native builds, exact original checkpoint training membership, larger independent evaluation and phone timings remain open. [Checks and blockers](quality/implementation-status.md) · [Benchmark reproduction](quality/benchmark.md) · [Setup](SETUP.md).

# Presentation direction and source notes

## Reference analysis

The linked profile is [Saishreek Singh / Yoriichi-GOD](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD). Its engineering archive uses original responsive artwork, working-interface specimens, concise project descriptions, maturity labels and direct links to evidence. Its strongest project pages keep unsuccessful measurements and unvalidated claims visible alongside working capabilities.

Repository presentation inspected on 14 November 2026:

| Reference | Pattern applied here |
| --- | --- |
| [Profile README](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD/Yoriichi-GOD/blob/98c8a259d7a2d5e409e44ca9ccda5e1d8614e77e/README.md) | Consistent artwork, concise positioning, actual UI and source links |
| [GhostTrace](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD/GhostTrace/blob/c827b06d9310c872e1334ed34a99dfb529f97e57/README.md) | Branded opening, readable purpose/status, reviewer route, evidence table and audience-specific links |
| [REFLEX](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD/REFLEX/blob/d32216c59f80e584a057602dc044539ce1b32d69/README.md) | A working inspection view and clear separation of measurement populations |
| [SatQuery](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD/SATquery-AI/blob/f53fa04e7e33ba6beddc72e7cb349a488261aa45/README.md) | Walkthrough/setup/architecture navigation, visual provenance and scoped claims |
| [Warscythe](https://github.com/Yoriichi-GOD/warscythe/blob/51cf4dc073af8484689722274792fc1e83a8f5a3/README.md) | A distinct project voice and concrete implementation explanations |

Links pin observed README-changing commits. This is a presentation analysis, not an independent audit of those projects.

## Applied to SafeSpace

The README now leads with original artwork, a clear purpose, current prototype status and an actual camera workspace. Four capabilities sit beside their interpretation limits. A narrow-screen capture shows the existing checklist. A short engineering explanation and evidence table lead to reviewer, architecture, setup and quality records.

Detailed setup/native/storage instructions remain in [SETUP.md](../SETUP.md); historical quality records stay at their original paths. The clone command selects the review branch because the work is still a draft PR. No hosted demo, verified APK, video, license or hidden-camera accuracy is invented.

The artwork uses SafeSpace's existing midnight, violet and cyan colours and shield motif. Reference logos, mascots, screenshots, text and code are not reused. [Media provenance](../media/README.md) records the actual capture scope.

The app UI, dependencies, model settings and four-tool journey are unchanged. Measurements retain their earlier quality-checkpoint attribution. After the local workspace became unavailable, temporary read-only CI capture tooling produced and formatted the documentation assets; it was removed from the final change.
